lead: the phone rings at all hours and it is never about anything you put up. twenty-six years of framing in four towns, and every call that comes in is somebody else's night going wrong.
sun: the trade keeps its memory in incidents. a job is remembered by the morning the joists moved, the argument on site, the winter a roof let go, and nothing you have framed has ever supplied one. four towns of your work sits inside finished walls carrying exactly what it was put there to carry, and the whole record of it is an absence of paperwork.
moon: The Gate spends itself entirely on other men's failures. the call comes in half-explained and you are already dressed and on a road at speed, and the trade's whole affection for you is made of those arrivals. nobody has ever had cause to send you to your own work, so the fastest part of you runs on how other people build.
pull: your name travels on other men's bad nights. everything of yours still standing has never handed a single person a reason to say it.
tension: the yard calls you steady, warmly, and steady is what gets said about a man there is no story about. quoting is where it bites: what wins the job is a rescue somebody remembers, the night you turned out for the school, the two days on the mill. thirty years of nothing happening in buildings a client has never been inside cannot be put on a page.
cost: a roof can be over a hundred people for thirty years and take up none of their thinking, which is the entire job and earns nothing extra — the arriving is paid at a premium and the standing goes on the metre rate like everybody else's. an apprentice learns this trade off disasters, so what the young ones copy off you is the callouts.

lead: nine years of it ended correctly, on paper, with a lunch afterwards. what has no ending written anywhere is the arrangement the four of you have lived inside ever since, and nobody has had occasion to name it.
sun: the family you came from is still one family, and what that rests on is open to inspection: who has whom at the holidays, which two are never in a room together, where the money from the house went. every part of it is in plain view and nobody has ever made a subject of it. it went up early, it carries, and something carrying properly gives nobody a reason to look at it.
moon: what you have is a sense of when. everything you have ever taken on came with a term and an hour it went over, and you pick the hour — news landing on the right evening, money released when the youngest was through school. your own position carries no term at all, so the one faculty you own has never found a date here to work on.
pull: you decide when everything in that family gets said. no right hour exists for the one item that is you, because a wall does not become the subject of an evening.
tension: your sister's account is that you took it all on because it suits you, and it goes unchallenged, since a structure turns out no evidence of effort. the file closed on time, which reads as competence rather than as nine years. requests arrive pre-arranged now — the summer week, the airport run, the question about the money — settled at your table by people with no sense of putting anything to anybody.
cost: terms set early and never once revisited are what keep four people who had every reason to stop speaking in each other's lives, and the terms have not taken an evening's worry off any of them. everything else you have held came with a delivery at the end. this is handed over to nobody, on no day, and the family's own version is that it all simply settled.

lead: one arrangement, and six policies inside it, and every person ever paid out of the thing believes they have been dealing with a consistent man.
sun: the arrangement went up when you were thirty and has not been altered since. four households take their rent out of it, a business got through two rough years on it, two courses were paid for, and none of it has ever been late. the papers sit in a drawer anyone in that family could open, and in twenty years nobody has, because opening it would be an event and nothing here has produced one.
moon: there are several of you making these decisions and they have never had to agree. one prices work at cost for a man he likes. one will not put the heating on in a cold house. one signed for a niece's fees inside a minute. The Gathered Stars supplies all six, the structure absorbs all six without registering a difference, and nothing has ever forced them into a policy.
pull: the payments have never varied by a day, which is how six different men in one body got twenty years of money behind them without ever once having to settle into one.
tension: two people who have had money out of you compared notes at a funeral and could not assemble one man from it. one was carried through a whole year; the other was refused two hundred and told to sort himself out. both accounts are exact. what settles it for everybody is that the payments have never missed, so being visibly solid is what stops the question getting asked, and there is no rule to give anyone who does.
cost: nothing has gone out late in twenty years, through two bad stretches nobody inside the arrangement noticed, and that is beyond most families and every committee. what can be handed on is a drawer and a total. the six of you who decided each of those payments were never reconciled into one, and the reasons went nowhere, so whoever inherits this gets a machine and no sense of it.

lead: you have been eleven pounds off a weight you set for yourself at twenty-four, every day since, and in all that time no part of the household has had to think about your body once.
sun: nothing that has never failed gets planned around; it gets assumed. twenty-nine years without a day lost, your father carried up those stairs for two winters, every shift covered including the ones nobody knew were covered — and none of that registers with the people it holds up, because their weeks are happening inside it rather than depending on it. a condition is not an event, and your body has never once been an event.
moon: inside, there is a distance that has not moved an inch. the weight was set by a version of yourself seen once, at twenty-four, and thirty years of pursuit has not closed on it and was never going to. the rules only accumulate: things get added to the list and nothing has ever come off. you would place in anything you entered, and you have entered nothing.
pull: the house has never once had to consider your body, and you have thought about almost nothing else since you were twenty-four.
tension: the plate goes out at their table, in front of five people, with the same two things on it, and in nine years nobody has remarked on it. disciplined gets said when anything gets said at all, and it lands as a compliment and closes the subject. the household's version of you is a man who does not eat much, and no evening has ever presented itself on which the chase could be mentioned.
cost: your children's whole account of childhood has no illness in it, no fortnight of a father in a chair, no arrangement ever rebuilt around him, and they experience that as ordinary weather. a pursuit like this keeps everything it picks up. the distance is the distance it was at twenty-four, it has cost you every meal you have eaten since, and there is no version of arriving.
